newsitem.title: HUNGARY: RAIFFEISEN UNICBANK H1 PROFITS EASE ON LOWER RATES.
newsitem.headline: RAIFFEISEN UNICBANK H1 PROFITS EASE ON LOWER RATES.

text.p: First half profits of Hungary's Raiffeisen Unicbank Rt eased year-on-year, due to falling interest rates and declining margins, Peter Felcsuti CEO of Raiffeisen Unicbank said on Monday.
The bank's profits before tax and provisions eased to 3.523 billion forints from 3.668 billion in the first six months of 1996.

In the first half of 1997 the bank's net interest income edged up to 4.045 billion forints from 4.034 billion forints in the same six months of 1996, meanwhile the bank sharply boosted both its lendings and its deposits to and from corporate clients.

Raiffeisen Unicbank's corporate lendings, including forint and foreign currencies, amounted to 102.077 billion forints from 70.247 billion in January-June 1996, while its deposits increased to 82.599 billion forints from 65.511 billion.

Interest margins of banks' forint transactions narrowed to around three percent from around six percent in about a half year, Felcsuti said, adding that this reflected the downward trend of interest rates.
"The direction of this trend did not surprise us, but its size certainly did," Felcsuti said about the falling margins.

Felcsuti, giving an overview of the Hungarian banking industry said the sector was stable but that competition was so fierce that banks can outperform others only by providing new and different services.

"A bank cannot distinguish itself by providing routine services only, it has to show something bigger added value," he said, referring to the need of combined financial packages and services requiring specialised knowledge," Felcsuti said.
"There's a very sharp competition, primarily for corporate clients."
He added average interest rates had fallen to around 20 percent from 26 to 27 percent last year.
Raiffeisen Unicbank Rt is a member of Austria's Raiffeisen Banking Group.
